comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** The new group check prevents the #3465 failure in both callers of the shared form. `useradd` refuses a login that matches an existing group because Arch's `login.defs` sets `USERGROUPS_ENAB yes`, and neither caller passes `-g`, `-N` or `-U`. `getent group` uses the same `getgrnam()` lookup. On first boot the check reads the same machine that `useradd` then runs on. On the ISO, every group the target has when archinstall runs `useradd` also exists on the live ISO, so no name that collides at that point gets through. The updated `test/shell.d/setup-form-test.sh` fails on the base form and passes on this head, and it no longer queries the host's group database.

| Name | Base form | This PR (ISO) | This PR (first boot) |
|---|---|---|---|
| `root` | reserved | reserved | reserved |
| `audio`, `wheel` | accepted, then `useradd` fails | rejected: group conflict | rejected: group conflict |
| existing user `dhh` | "already exists" (first boot) | n/a | "already exists" (checked before the group lookup) |
| `david` | accepted | accepted | accepted |

### `docker` is still accepted on the ISO and becomes the account's primary group

The new comment in `install/provisioning/setup-form.sh` and the PR description give `docker` as a name that is now rejected. That holds only on first boot. On the ISO, the `docker` group does not exist yet when the form runs or when the account is created:

```text
ISO configurator (live ISO)   getent group docker -> not found -> name accepted
target: early packages        no docker group
target: create_users          useradd -m -G wheel -- docker
                              USERGROUPS_ENAB yes -> creates group "docker" as the primary group
target: omarchy-base.packages docker package, sysusers "g docker - -" -> group already exists, skipped
result                        login "docker" is in group docker (primary); docker.socket is SocketGroup=docker, 0660
```

`plocate` (`g locate 21 - -`) follows the same path for the name `locate`. This behavior predates the PR (the base form accepts these names too), but the new comment says the case is covered.

**Impact:** A user who picks `docker` as a login on an ISO install gets access to the Docker daemon socket without sudo, although Omarchy leaves Docker access opt-in. Removing it later with `gpasswd -d` does not work on a primary group. The traced path is from source; an installed image was not checked.

**Suggested change:** Add `docker` and `locate` to `OMARCHY_RESERVED_USERNAMES`. The reserved list does not depend on which environment runs the form. Also reword the comment: neither caller passes `-U` (the behavior comes from `USERGROUPS_ENAB`), and on the ISO the lookup only sees groups that already exist on the live ISO.

**Note, ISO also rejects some names the target would accept:** The live ISO has groups that the target does not have when the account is created, for example `openvpn`, `dnsmasq`, `named`, `dhcpcd`, `nbd`, `rpcuser`, `usbmux`, `vboxsf`, `partimag` and `brlapi`. The ISO form now rejects these names, although `useradd` on the target would accept them. The user sees a clear notice and picks another name, so the practical cost is small. The list comes from package metadata for the current stable channel, not from a booted ISO.

**Optional:** `bin/omarchy-provision-owner` redefines `omarchy_username_conflicts_group` with the same body as the `setup-form.sh` version it already sources. The copy changes nothing and could drift, so it can be removed.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Source review of this head, archinstall 4.4, shadow 4.20.0 (Arch packaging), glibc `getent`, the omarchy-iso `quattro` orchestrator and the Arch package definitions involved. The shell test was run against the base form and this head. The production helpers were exercised with a scripted `gum` and a synthetic passwd/group database. No real `useradd`, ISO install or first boot was run, so the `useradd` outcomes above come from source.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, independent Opus 5.5 Xhigh and GPT 6 Sol Xhigh technical assessments with targeted follow-up questions, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.
